summary: Loved for its tactile dials, colours, sharp files and the fun of using it, in a body lighter than most full frame. The main complaint is autofocus that trails Sony, Canon and Nikon on moving subjects, followed by finish and build issues such as scratching paint and a plastic feel. Suits stills, travel and street more than sports.

Most reviewers praise sticky, fast autofocus, strong low-light files and handling that suits long shoots, with good battery life, dual card slots and in-body stabilisation. Complaints are scattered: some find the colours dull or greenish, a few want more than 24MP for cropping, and the electronic shutter shows rolling shutter. Suits sports, wildlife and hybrid shooters.

Many wildlife and sports shooters like its crop reach, comfortable grip, good value and, for some, fast autofocus. The main complaint is inconsistent autofocus, especially in low light, clutter or fast bursts, and several sold it for a full-frame body. Rolling shutter with the electronic shutter and noisier low-light files than full frame also come up.

Praised for its sharp lens, high-resolution image quality, simple menus and build, and it is a favourite travel camera. Autofocus is the main complaint, weaker on tracking and moving kids, though firmware 4.0 improved it for many. Some find the 28mm too wide, the body big for a compact, or the JPEGs needing edits.

Praised for putting full-frame quality and good low-light performance in a very light, compact body at a fair price. Recurring downsides are small battery life, overheating in video, and a rubber grip that wears or peels. Some miss in-body stabilisation, and the small body can feel cramped. Suits travel and hobbyists.

Impresses most reviewers with clean image quality, strong low light, good colours and a handy detachable screen. Overheating is the leading complaint, with shutdowns during long 4K clips, followed by firmware and build glitches and weak battery life. The missing webcam mode also disappoints some. Better for shorter clips than long recording.

Loved for its small size, colours and film simulations, and many carry it everywhere. Autofocus is the biggest complaint, with owners coming from Sony or Canon finding it slow or unreliable for kids, low light and video, and the fixed lens limits some. A few mention build faults and battery life. Suits street and travel.

Gets praise for its deep grip, long battery life, colours straight out of camera and strong video features in a small body. Overheating in video and heat is the top complaint, followed by autofocus that lags rivals on fast subjects and build some find loose or flimsy. Suits hybrid and travel shooters more than action.

Mostly praised for strong low-light 360 video, sharp image quality and replaceable lenses. Downsides are bulk and weight, awkward on helmets and bikes, some build failures, heating at 8K, and slow, laborious editing and software. Single-lens mode helps some but trails dedicated action cameras.

Loved as a pocketable everyday camera with a sharp zoom lens, physical dials, a good viewfinder and pleasing Leica colours. Complaints centre on the high price for a small, older sensor that limits low light and cropping, slow start-up, and a few build faults such as dust in the lens or sensor. Suits casual travel and street.

Valued for its build, battery life, USB-C charging, image quality and engaging rangefinder shooting. The main complaint is random freezing and lost or corrupted files, often improved by firmware updates or the right SD card, plus a magenta cast some find hard to edit. The rangefinder is hard for fast-moving subjects. Suits deliberate shooters.

Loved mainly as a small, premium-feeling camera with interchangeable lenses and sharp, crop-friendly files, and many call it their favourite carry-around. Downsides include weak battery life, a small EVF and touchy eye sensor, no weather sealing, and cramped handling without a grip. A few report overheating or slow wake.

Loved for its exceptionally sharp APO lens, rich image quality and simple, enjoyable handling in a compact fixed-lens body. Autofocus is the main complaint, with those coming from Sony or Canon finding it slow or unreliable on moving subjects, though firmware improved it. The 43mm view feels tight for crowds and kids. Suits street and portraits.

Liked for fast, reliable autofocus, excellent low-light files and a retro, dial-driven design that is fun to shoot. The common complaint is weight and ergonomics: the shallow grip is awkward with larger lenses, so many add a grip, and a few sold it as too heavy or uncomfortable. The flip-out screen and few custom options also irk some.

Praised for superb subject-tracking autofocus in a compact body, with good battery life, strong high-ISO results and plenty of lens choice. The main downside is overheating in long 4K video. A few miss the third dial or joystick, find it barely smaller than full frame, or find the JPEGs only competent. Suits travel, wildlife and hybrid shooters.

Owners love the compact, solid rangefinder experience, bright viewfinder and detailed files, and many call it a favourite camera. The leading complaint is freezing plus firmware and SD card trouble, though many say it stopped after updates or a card change. Manual focus misses shots on moving kids, and the 60MP sensor is demanding. Suits slow, deliberate shooting.

Seen as a cheap, light way into full frame, with good low-light results and lovely stills for portraits, landscapes and travel. Common drawbacks are weak battery life, older autofocus and slow burst that struggle with sports, wildlife and video, and a few report poor build. Suits slower subjects on a budget.

Praised for being tiny and light with good image quality and colours, making it a popular everyday and travel camera, often with a pancake lens. The most common regret is the missing viewfinder, hard to live with in bright sun, and some find it cheaply built or cramped to hold. Suits casual carry or second-body use.

Liked for its tiny magnetic hands-free design and good daylight quality, with better low light than the GO 3S for some. The main complaints are poor battery life, notably the detached camera draining while idle, plus overheating, and a few units dying after sitting or being lost off the magnetic mount. Dim-light footage is mixed.

Liked as one of the smallest full-frame cameras, with autofocus many call near automatic, strong image quality and good low light. It is popular for travel and hiking with small primes. Downsides are few: some find it front-heavy with big lenses, miss a bigger grip, buttons or viewfinder, and the single card slot worries some.
